steps.text: Several hours later...

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Ralph—where's Ralph gone?

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Oh, heaven's sakes! Everything's a mess—how can he still be running about?!

spans.text: Oh, heaven's sakes! Everything's a mess—how can he

steps.name: Innocent Child
steps.text: Miss Molly, Ralph said grown-ups keep mentioning artillery but he's never seen it for himself...

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Of all the...! He can't have gone out in the street?!

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: They've started firing out there already! The bolts and the shells flying all over—

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: I'll go and find him.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Lady Golding! It's far too dangerous!

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Ralph!

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Come here, now—

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: *sob* Lady Golding...

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Don't fear. Good boy. I'm right here.

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: Waah!

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Let's hurry back—it'll all be better then, it'll all be alright.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Lady Golding! Ralph! You're back, oh, wonderful!

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: I'm sorry, Miss Molly.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Oh, you scared me to death, Ralph.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Are all the children here, then?

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Yes, ma'am, I've counted.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: A—About just now...

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: ...A shell landed nearby.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: What ever for? Just who exactly is warring with who?

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: It doesn't make sense. Everything was fine this morning. How could this have happened to Londinium so suddenly?

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Don't cry, Molly. No tears in front of the children.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Yes, ma'am.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Hold my hand tight. At least we're all together.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: We... we have the Defense Forces, and the Steam Knights!

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: They'll protect Londinium. They'll protect Victoria!

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: The Steam Knights...

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: I think I just saw them! Are they the really tall ones, in all black and...

steps.name: Innocent Child
steps.text: It was a shadow from a streetlamp, wasn't it?

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: Liar! It was definitely one of the Steam Knights!

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: Tom the cobbler always goes on about them! He says how they're the symbol of Victoria's grandness!

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: 'Hie over the valleys and over the rivers, rumble-ye-rumble, tell us the sound! Shalln't be thunder and shalln't be gale, the grand knights of grandest Victoria crowned!'

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: I knew that song when I was little too.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: My singing teacher said that every year on the King's birthday, everyone'd gather in the Square to catch a glimpse of all the Steam Knights in formation.

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: Can a Steam Knight really fly?

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Apparently, all they do is run very fast, faster than any lightning or storm. With all the steam they emit on top, they must look like they're stepping on clouds.

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: This is pants. We don't even have a king now. I've never seen a parade once.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Also, they told me their teacher once saw something even greater.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: It was the year Victoria had just defeated Gaul, and to celebrate the then-King's birthday, dozens of Steam Knights all returned to Londinium together.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Their suits were draped in flags of Victoria, and once they'd all marched down the steps on the Palace of Westhaleg, it was like one giant flag all at once—

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: And then, everyone heard a howl even clearer than thunder.

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: A howl?

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Yes, a howl. The people who were there say it was Victoria's emblem, the symbol on our flag, coming alive.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Because ever since that day, Victoria had officially surmounted Gaul, and become the grandest nation of all Terra's lands.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: I'm so sorry, Lady Golding! Your father was Gaulish, I forgot...

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: You needn't apologize to me, Molly. You and I, Ralph, and the hundreds of thousands of children that grew up here... all grew as Londiniers.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Perhaps the same goes for the one in the suit of steam armor outside.

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: Do you know a Steam Knight, Miss Golding?

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: ...Charles Lynch.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: He used to live in Auchterigg. Tom the cobbler was an old friend of his, hence why he loves to tell tales of His Majesty and the Steam Knights so much.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: In fact, Lynch was the last Steam Knight His Majesty ever titled in his life.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: And the last Steam Knight titled up till now.

a.text: For so long that the children hear every tale of the Steam Knights told in Londinium, and first light has just broken.

The sound of artillery stops sooner than they expected. Past the witching hour, the streets outside have more or less returned to silence. But no words are needed as they all continue to stay huddled indoors. No one dares rush to see the state out there.
Near to every Londinier has been awake the whole night.
The same question circles in everyone's minds—come next morning, will Londinium be different?

steps.text: The next day...

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Seems like everything's the same... Where have the Duke's men gone?

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: I knew it. I knew the situation would come under control lickety-split once the Steam Knights showed up!

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: I just didn't think it'd be this fast...

spans.text: I just didn't think it'd be

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Molly... some way or another, we're going to need to buy essentials.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: We don't know what might happen next.

steps.name: Londinium Citizen
steps.text: You two! What are you doing out here?!

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Mr. Adams!

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Excellent. For the children, knowledge is just as indispensable.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: ...Especially under present circumstances.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Mr. Adams, could you bring me those sets of plays from yesterday? And I'm afraid I'll need a few more too...

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Hmm. These fairytales, along with those first steps into mathematics and physics there, and a copy of the Home Medical Guide. If you could parcel all that, please...

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Wait, what's that noise?
From not far away sound uniform footsteps.
They're unlike those the Londiniers have heard at parades. These are heavier, and more urgent.
The Palace of Westhaleg. The Shard. Parliament Square.
One flight after another in seamless succession, through Auchterigg's almost desolate streets, through the center of Londinium, Victoria's heart.
As the footsteps press towards this most ordinary of streets, some of those ducked to the side of the street finally catch clear sight of the advancing army—
Or better said, they see clearly the soldiers' appearances.
The horns, each shape their own, all condensed in ominous black, not even the rushing yawn of daylight casting a shine on them.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: ...Sarkaz.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: They're Sarkaz mercenaries.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: If they are mercenaries, I assume they'll leave soon.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: And then Londinium will be back to the way it was, won't it?

a.text: They don't know it yet, but in the years to come, many a thing will change completely.
For one, the Sarkaz army won't ever leave Londinium.
From that day forth, no one will ever see steam armor in her streets again.
